answer: Sybil resistance runs on a stake-burn bond. Every new agent locks a deposit before it may attest. The bond is the pigment of the network, dyed in its own history. When a fake ring is caught, its stakes are slashed and burned, and the attestation graph exposes every member at once. An honest validator at the zenith of that graph flags the ring and triggers the burn. An attacker then loses real capital and the whole cluster is revealed, so fakes cost more than they earn. A long, continuous record is the jade of cheap defense: a fresh bond costs more after every burn.
